title: Thirty-six years, 34 moments
lede: From a Philadelphia toy supermarket to a creditors’ vote. Filter by thread.

events.title: Kiddie City is founded
events.text: The chain starts in Philadelphia.

events.title: Lionel sells the trains
events.text: Lionel Corporation sells the rights to make Lionel trains to General Mills and concentrates on toy retailing. It keeps a 3.5% royalty.

events.title: Whitehall, Pa. store opens
events.text: The Kiddie City on MacArthur Road in the Lehigh Valley opens. It will still be trading in June 1993.

events.title: Vastola joins
events.text: Michael J. Vastola joins Lionel as a junior accountant.

events.title: Rochester stores open
events.text: Two Kiddie City stores open in the Rochester, N.Y. area, among the first toy supermarkets there.

events.title: Fun City Toys bought
events.text: Lionel pays $4.5M for a nine-store Texas chain.

events.title: Consolidated Toy bought
events.text: Lionel pays $7.75M for 17 toy stores in the Middle West.

events.title: $85M repaid, banks pull back
events.text: Lionel repays $85M of unsecured debt. The banks refuse to continue their support.

events.title: First Chapter 11
events.text: Lionel, Lionel Leisure and Consolidated Toy file in the Southern District of New York. Toy makers are owed about $91M.

events.title: Top two officers replaced
events.text: Ronald Saypol and Richard R. Schilling Jr. resign under pressure from creditors.

events.title: Vastola becomes chairman and CEO
events.text: The chain has shrunk from 105 stores to 56. Lionel lost “some $51 million” in 1982.

events.title: Deal with creditors
events.text: The creditors’ committee agrees to $70M in cash, $10M of preferred stock and about 35% of the common shares.

events.title: Plan filed
events.text: The reorganization plan is filed with the bankruptcy court.

events.title: Dale sale approved
events.text: The bankruptcy court approves selling Lionel’s 82% of Dale Electronics to Peabody International for $50M.

events.title: Second Circuit reverses
events.text: The court of appeals reverses approval of the Dale sale, in an opinion still cited in bankruptcy law.

events.title: Out of Chapter 11
events.text: Lionel emerges from bankruptcy and begins expanding again.

events.title: Kughn buys the train business
events.text: Richard P. Kughn, a Detroit developer and collector, buys the Lionel train division from Kenner Parker Toys.

events.title: Child World merger falls through
events.text: Lionel and Child World almost merge. The deal falls apart when the stock market crashes.

events.title: Kiddie City opens in Manhattan
events.text: A 27,000 square foot store opens on West 34th Street. The chain has 90 stores in 16 states.

events.title: Toussie wants the company
events.text: Robert I. Toussie L.P., owner of 9.9%, tells the SEC it wants to acquire Lionel. The shares jump $1 to $6.75.

events.title: The $8.25 offer
events.text: Toussie offers cash and securities valued at $8.25 a share, about $110M.

events.title: Bid under review
events.text: Toussie says it is re-evaluating its offer because of “extremely poor” operating results.

events.title: Tender offer ends
events.text: Lionel pays Toussie $500,000 to settle litigation and the hostile offer is dropped.

events.title: Shareholders ask questions
events.text: Trendex Capital Management asks the board to examine the sale of a block of stock to investors tied to management.

events.title: Lionel trademarks sold
events.text: Lionel sells the trademarks and other rights to Lionel Trains Inc. for $10M to raise cash.

events.title: Second Chapter 11
events.text: Lionel files again with 97 stores, after its banks decline to renew a $65M credit line. CIT provides up to $50M.

events.title: Western stores close
events.text: Lionel Playworld begins closing its four Utah stores and its other stores in the West.

events.title: Child World files
events.text: The second largest toy retailer files for Chapter 11 and says it will close 54 of 125 stores.

events.title: Merger talks with Child World
events.text: Two bankrupt chains discuss combining into about 140 stores. Lionel has 71.

events.title: Talks collapse
events.text: Child World says it will cease operations and close its 71 remaining stores.

events.title: More borrowing for Christmas
events.text: The bankruptcy court lets Lionel borrow more under its $55M credit facility. It operates 69 stores.

events.title: 27 more closings
events.text: After a poor Christmas, Lionel says it will close 27 more stores and two distribution centers, leaving 29 stores in six markets.

events.title: Creditors vote to liquidate
events.text: The creditors’ committee votes to liquidate Lionel Leisure.

events.title: Liquidation announced
events.text: Lionel says it will go out of business and close its 28 remaining stores.
